Rashi on Pesachim 61b:10:1.hebrew: וכי תימא מאי חומרא דזריקה - משחיטה, דמוקמית קולא דמקצת ערלה לא פסלה אשחיטה, אבל זריקה אפי' מקצתה פסלה? היינו חומרא דילה, דלא מקיים פיגול אלא בזריקה. אם חישב באחת מארבע עבודות על מנת לאכול הימנו כזית חוץ לזמנו, פיגול הוא, וחייבין עליו כרת אפילו אכל ממנו תוך זמנו, כדכתיב (ויקרא ו) "והנפש האוכלת ממנו עונה תשא", ובלבד שיעשו כל עבודות שלאחריה שלא בפסול אחר, אלא או בשתיקה, או בכשרות — על מנת תוך זמנו — או על מנת פיגול כמותה. אבל חישב באחת מעבודות שלאחריה פסול אחר, כגון חוץ למקומו, שוב אין בו כרת, כדאמרי' בזבחים (דף כח:) ובמנחות בפרק שני (דף טז.): הרצאה כתיבה בפיגול — נאמר "לא ירצה" בפיגול, ונאמר בכשר "מיום השמיני והלאה ירצה" — כהרצאת כשר כך הרצאת פיגול: מה הרצאת כשר עד שיקרבו כל מתיריו בכשרות, אף הרצאת פיגול עד שיקרבו כל מתיריו או בפיגול או בכשרות. אלמא לא מיקבע וודאי של פיגול אלא בזריקה שהיא סוף העבודה, דכל שעתא קאי בספק שמא יחשב פסול אחר בעבודה הבאה ויפקיע שם פיגול ממנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:10:1.english: And if you say: What is the stringency of sprinkling - [over] slaughter, that you establish the leniency that partial uncircumcision does not disqualify [the offering] at slaughter, whereas [at] sprinkling even partial [uncircumcision] disqualifies? This is its stringency: that piggul is not established except at sprinkling. If one had intent during one of the four [essential] services to eat an olive-bulk of it beyond its [allotted] time, it is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it even if one ate from it within its [allotted] time — as it is written (Leviticus 6): "And the soul that eats of it shall bear its iniquity" — provided that all the services following it are performed without any other disqualification, but rather either in silence [i.e., with no specific intent], or with valid [intent] — [i.e.,] to [eat it] within its [allotted] time — or with piggul [intent] like it. However, [if] one had intent of another disqualification during one of the services following it, such as [eating it] outside its [designated] place, there is no longer karet for it, as we say in Zevachim (28b) and in Menachot in the second chapter (16a): "Acceptance" is written regarding piggul — it is stated "it shall not be accepted" regarding piggul, and it is stated regarding a valid [offering], "from the eighth day onward it shall be accepted" — just as the acceptance of a valid [offering], so is the acceptance of piggul: just as the acceptance of a valid [offering] [takes effect only] when all of its permitting rites are offered in validity, so too the acceptance of piggul [takes effect only] when all of its permitting rites are offered either as piggul or in validity. Thus, the certainty of piggul is not established until sprinkling, which is the end of the service, for at every moment it stands in doubt lest one have intent of another disqualification in the next service and thereby remove the status of piggul from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:11:1.hebrew: מתקיף לה רב אשי - בין לרבה בין לרב חסדא, ממאי דהאי "וכל ערל" עד דאיכא כולה ערלה משמע, דנייתי "זאת" למעוטי זריקה למר לחומרא ולמר לקולא, ות"ל "זאת" דקתני תנא מילתא אחריתי קאמר? דילמא "זאת" דקתני תנא, אמילתיה קאי, ומינה יליף דאינו פוסל בני חבורה הבאין עמו, ומשום ד"כל ערל" כל דהו משמע. והכי קאמר: יכול יפסול בני חבורה, ד"כל ערל" כל דהו משמע, ושוב לא יאכל בו שום אדם:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:11:1.english: Rav Ashi strongly objects to it - According to both Rabbah and Rav Chisda: From where [do you know] that this [phrase] "and any uncircumcised [male]" implies [that the offering is not disqualified] until there is complete uncircumcision, such that "this" comes to exclude sprinkling — according to one [opinion] stringently and according to the other [opinion] leniently — and [that] "the verse teaches: 'This'" which the Tanna taught is saying another matter? Perhaps "this" that the Tanna taught refers to its own matter, and from it he derives that he does not disqualify the members of the group who come with him, because "any uncircumcised [male]" implies any amount. And this is what [the Tanna] is saying: "One might think that he disqualifies the members of the group" — since "any uncircumcised [male]" implies any amount — "and thus no person may eat of it [anymore]."

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:11:2.hebrew: ת"ל זאת - עבודה שלימה בעינן בערלות, ולעולם לא שנא שחיטה ולא שנא זריקה, שוין:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:11:2.english: Scripture states, "This" - We require a complete service in [a state of] uncircumcision [to disqualify the offering], and in all cases, there is no difference between slaughtering and sprinkling — [they are] equal.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:1:1.hebrew: שחטו - להאכילו למולין מנויין, אבל יתכפרו בו בזריקתו ערלים, או מנויין או שאינן מנויין:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:1:1.english: He slaughtered it - To feed it to circumcised [people who are] registered [for it], but [with the intent that] uncircumcised [people] should achieve atonement through it via its sprinkling, whether [they are] registered or not registered.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:1:2.hebrew: אין מחשבת ערלים בזריקה - לא מהני לפסול, וטעמא מפרש לקמיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:1:2.english: There is no intent [for] uncircumcised [people] during the sprinkling - It is not effective to disqualify [the offering], and [the Gemara] explains the reason further on.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:1.hebrew: מנא אמינא לה כו' - רישא דברייתא, "וכל ערל לא יאכל בו":
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:1.english: From where do I say it, etc. - The beginning of the baraita [is]: "And no uncircumcised person shall eat of it."

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:2.english: [One] might [think] he would disqualify - An uncircumcised person.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:3.hebrew: בני חבורה הבאין עמו - שאם נמנו עליו מולין וערל שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה, ושחט לשם כולם, יכול יפסל:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:3.english: The members of the group who come with him - For if circumcised [individuals] and an uncircumcised [man] whose brothers died due to circumcision were registered on [the Paschal offering], and [one] slaughtered [it] for the sake of all of them, one might [have thought that it] would be disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:4.hebrew: הואיל וטומאה פוסלת - אם שחטו לטמאין, דבעינן הראוי לאוכלו, כדכתיב: "איש לפי אכלו תכוסו" — תשחטו. ולתנא קמא, דלית ליה לשון סורסי, בתריה כתיב: "ושחטו אותו":
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:4.english: Since ritual impurity disqualifies - If one slaughtered it for ritually impure [people], since we require [one] who is fit to eat it, as it is written: "according to every man's eating you shall make your count [takhosu]" — [meaning] "you shall slaughter." And according to the Tanna Kamma, who does not hold [this interpretation from] the Syriac language, afterward it is written: "and they shall slaughter it."

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:5.english: And lack of circumcision disqualifies - For this reason as well, [namely] that we require [one who is] fit to eat [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:6.english: Just as [with] ritual impurity, partial impurity was not made [like full impurity] - For example, [when it is slaughtered] for ritually impure [people] and for ritually pure [people].

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:7.hebrew: ככל טומאה - כאילו נשחט כולו לטמאים. ולקמן פריך: מאי שנא טומאה דפשיטא ליה, ומאי שנה ערלה דמספקא ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:2:7.english: Like full impurity - As if it were slaughtered entirely for impure [people]. And later [the Gemara] asks: What is different [about] impurity that it is obvious to him, and what is different [about] lack of circumcision that it is uncertain to him?

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:3:1.hebrew: וזמן פוסל - שחטו על מנת לאכול הימנו כזית חוץ לזמנו, נעשה כולו פיגול, והיינו "מקצת זמן", שלא חישב אלא על כזית הימנו, כדכתיב "אם האכל יאכל וגו'". ותניא בתורת כהנים ובזבחים (דף כט.): כוף אזנך לשמוע — במחשב לאכול מזבחו ביום השלישי הכתוב מדבר, וכתיב "האכל יאכל" — אכילה בכזית:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:3:1.english: And time disqualifies - [If] he slaughtered it with the intention to eat an olive's bulk of it beyond its [allotted] time, the entire [offering] becomes piggul [disqualified due to improper time-intent]; and this is [what is meant by] "partial time," for he only intended [this] regarding an olive's bulk of it, as it is written: "If it is eaten at all, etc." And it is taught in Torat Kohanim and in Zevachim (29a): "Incline your ear to hear — Scripture speaks of one who intends to eat from his sacrifice on the third day, and it is written 'eaten, it shall be eaten' — eating is [at least] an olive's bulk."

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:3:2.hebrew: ערלה וטומאה אינה נוהגת בשאר זבחים כפסח, שכן ערל וטמא משלחין קרבנותיהן, דלא מעכבא בהו אכילת בעלים:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:3:2.english: Lack of circumcision and ritual impurity do not apply to other sacrifices as [they do] to the Paschal offering, for an uncircumcised person or an impure person may send their sacrifices [to be offered], since eating by the owners is not essential for them.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:5:1.hebrew: ערלה לא הותרה מכללה - שאין שום קרבן נאכל לערלים, דילפינן ביבמות (דף עג.) דערל אסור בקדשים, דאתי בקל וחומר מפסח הקל. וזמן נמי לא הותר לשום קרבן לאוכלו חוץ לזמנו. וטומאה הותרה מכללה, כדמפרש לקמן: הפסח שבא בטומאה נאכל בטומאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:5:1.english: [The law of] uncircumcision has no exception from its rule - For no sacrifice may be eaten by uncircumcised [males], as we derive in Yevamot (73a) that an uncircumcised [male] is forbidden [to eat] sacrificial foods, for it is derived by a kal va-chomer (a fortiori inference) from the Pesach [offering], which is [more] lenient. And [regarding] time as well: no sacrifice is permitted to be eaten beyond its [allotted] time. Whereas ritual impurity has an exception from its rule, as [the Gemara] explains below: the Pesach [offering] that is brought in [a state of] ritual impurity may be eaten in [a state of] ritual impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:6:1.hebrew: ת"ל זאת - חקת הפסח, וכתיב בההיא פרשתא: ״כל ערל לא יאכל בו״:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:6:1.english: The verse states: “This” - [“This is] the ordinance of the Passover,” and it is written in that section: “no uncircumcised [male] shall eat of it.”

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:6:2.hebrew: מאי זאת - היכי משמע מזאת דאינו פוסל בני חבורה הבאין עמו? על כרחיך מילתא אחריתי קאמר, והכי קאמר: ת"ל וכל ערל — עד דאיכא כולה ערלות, וזאת אתא דלא תימא הוא הדין לזריקה, דכולה ערלות מיהא פסלה ביה, אם שחטו למולין על מנת לזרוק דמה לערלים לבדם:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:6:2.english: What [is meant by] "this"? - How is it implied from "this" that it does not disqualify the members of the group who come with him? Perforce, [the Gemara] is saying something else, and this is what it is saying: The verse states "and every uncircumcised male" — [teaching that it is not disqualified] until there is complete uncircumcision [among the group]; and "this" comes [to teach] that you should not say the same applies to sprinkling [the blood], that complete uncircumcision at least disqualifies it if one slaughtered it for circumcised [people] with the intent to sprinkle its blood for uncircumcised [people] alone.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:7:1.hebrew: תלמוד לומר זאת - דמשמע בעבודה א' הוא דפסלה ערלות, והיינו שחיטה, דהיא תחלה לעבודות, והיא הוזכרה אצל מנויין ואוכלין, כדמפרש:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:7:1.english: The verse states: “This” - Which implies [that] it is in one service [only] that uncircumcision disqualifies, and that is slaughter, for it is the first of the services, and it was mentioned in connection with those registered [for the offering] and those who eat [it], as [the Gemara] explains.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:8:1.hebrew: וכ"ת מאי קולא דזריקה - דתימא האי "זאת" אשחיטה קאי ולמעוטי זריקה, היינו קולא: דהא לא אתרבי מחשבת אוכלין אצל זריקה, דשחיטה גלי בה רחמנא. הלכך, מסתברא ד"זאת" דפסול כולה ערלות אשחיטה קאי ולאו אזריקה, ו"זאת" משמע מיעוטא:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:8:1.english: And if you say: What is the leniency of sprinkling - [That] you say this [word] "this" [zot] refers to slaughtering, and to exclude sprinkling — this is the leniency: for intent concerning those who may eat was not included with respect to sprinkling, since the Merciful One revealed [it] regarding slaughtering. Therefore, it stands to reason that "this" [zot], regarding the disqualification of [an offering for a group that is] entirely uncircumcised, refers to slaughtering and not to sprinkling, and "this" [zot] implies an exclusion.

Rashi on Pesachim 61b:9:1.hebrew: ורב חסדא - דאמר לעיל יש מחשבת (אוכלין) [ערלים] בזריקה, אמר לך: האי זאת לאו לקולא גבי זריקה הוא, אלא לאחמורי עליה אתא, והכא קאמר: זאת היא דמקצת ערלה לא פסלה בה, אבל זריקה, אפילו מקצתה פסלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 61b:9:1.english: And Rav Ḥisda - who said above [that] there is [disqualifying] intent regarding uncircumcised persons during sprinkling, would say to you: this [word] "this" is not [meant] for leniency regarding sprinkling, rather it comes to be stringent upon it, and here [the verse] says: this [slaughter] is what partial uncircumcision does not disqualify, but [regarding] sprinkling, even part of it disqualifies.

Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:11:1.hebrew: דילמא האי כל ערל אפילו כל דהו - אע"ג דפלוגתא דתנאי הוא בסנהדרין (ד' עח.) גבי הכוהו עשרה בני אדם בי' מקלות בכל נפש, אי כולה נפש משמע או כל דהו, וכן בבכורות (ד' ג.) גבי כל בכור — רב אשי בא לסתור ראייתו של רבה ולהעמיד הברייתא כמאן דאמר כל דהו משמע. ועוד, כדפי' בקונטרס, דברייתא גופה מוכחא דזאת בא להתיר מקצת ערלות, ולהכי פריך:
Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:11:1.english: Perhaps this [phrase] "any uncircumcised [male]" [means] even any amount - Even though it is a dispute of Tannaim in Sanhedrin (78a) regarding [the case where] ten people struck him with ten sticks, [concerning the verse] "any soul [kol nefesh]," whether it means the entire soul or any amount, and similarly in Bekhorot (3a) regarding "any firstborn [kol bekhor]" — Rav Ashi comes to refute Rabbah's proof and to establish the Baraita according to the one who says [that kol] means any amount. And furthermore, as Rashi explained, the Baraita itself proves that "this" comes to permit partial uncircumcision, and therefore [Rav Ashi] objects:

Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:11:2.hebrew: כתב רחמנא זאת עד דאיכא כולה ערלה - תימה: לשתוק מ"כל"! ועוד, דנימא איפכא: ד"זאת" ודאי כולה ערלה משמע, כתב רחמנא "כל" — אפילו כל דהו! וי"ל דידע בעל הש"ס דאיצטריך "כל" לשום דרשה אחריתי, ואיצטריך "זאת" לגלויי דלא נדרוש מ"כל" כל דהו; אבל אי הוה דרשי' איפכא, לא הוה ידעינן כלל "זאת" למאי אתא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:11:2.english: The Merciful One wrote "this [zot]," [teaching] that until there is all [of it] uncircumcised - This is astonishing: let [Scripture] be silent from [writing] "all [kol]"! And furthermore, let us say the opposite: that "this [zot]" certainly implies all [of it] uncircumcised, [and] the Merciful One wrote "all [kol]" — [to teach] even any amount! And one can say that the author of the Talmud knew that "all [kol]" is needed for a different exposition, and "this [zot]" is needed to reveal that we should not expound "any amount" from "all [kol]"; however, if we had expounded the opposite, we would not know at all what "this [zot]" came for.

Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:1:1.hebrew: שחטו למולין על מנת שיתכפרו בו ערלים - אם שחטו למנויו על מנת שיתכפרו בו שאינם מנויו, הא פשיטא דפסול לכ"ע, דהיינו שינוי בעלים דפסול בפסח ובחטאת. ומיהו נראה לר"י דה"נ פליגי בשחט לאוכליו על מנת שיתכפרו שאינם אוכלין, כגון חולה וזקן, דפסל ביה רב חסדא כמו בערלים, אע"ג דקראי דמייתי בערל כתיבי, דמחד קרא ד"לפי אכלו" נפקי וילפי מהדדי לכל מילי; דהא לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו דכשר, היינו משום דילפי' מלמולים ולערלים. ודווקא בשחט למולים ע"מ שיתכפרו ערלים פסל רב חסדא, אבל נזרק לשם ערלים — אפי' רב חסדא מודה דכשר, דאין מחשבת אוכלין בזריקה; דהא בכ"מ פשוט זה למסדר הש"ס בכולה שמעתי'. ובריש זבחים (ד' ד.) דקאמר: "אשכחן זביחה, שאר עבודות מנלן? וכי תימא נילף מזביחה — מה לזביחה שכן פסולה שלא לשם אוכלין בפסח", משמע דליכא מאן דפליג דאין מחשבת אוכלין בזריקה. ועוד, דרב אשי מסיק דרבה לא פליג בהא אדרב חסדא. ובפ' כיצד צולין (פסחים ד' עח.) דתניא: "שחטו לאוכליו לזרוק דמו שלא לאוכליו — פסח עצמו כשר ואדם יוצא בו ידי חובתו", לא גרסינן "לזרוק דמו" אלא "ונזרק דמו", דלא תיקשי לרב חסדא, וכן יש במקצת ספרים. וריב"א פי' דדוקא נקט "על מנת שיתכפרו" — שחישב להתכפר בו ערלים, אבל אם לא חישב להתכפר, אלא חישב לזרוק להאכיל הבשר לערלים — אפי' רב חסדא מודה דכשר, דלא שייך בזריקה מחשבת פסול דאכילה אלא פסול דכפרה; ובשחיטה דווקא אם חישב להאכיל שלא לאוכליו ולערלים פסול, דשחיטה ודאי בעינן לשם בעלים הראויים לאוכלו, כדכתיב: "איש לפי אכלו תכוסו", והיינו דאין מחשבת אוכלין בזריקה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:1:1.english: If he slaughtered it for circumcised [people] on condition that uncircumcised [people] achieve atonement through it - If he slaughtered it for its registered [members] on condition that those who are not its registered [members] achieve atonement through it, it is obvious that it is disqualified according to all opinions, for this is a change of owners [shinui be'alim], which is disqualifying in a Paschal offering and in a sin-offering. However, it appears to Ri that they similarly disagree where he slaughtered [it] for its eaters on condition that non-eaters — such as a sick person or an elderly person — achieve atonement [through it], where Rav Ḥisda disqualifies it just as with uncircumcised [people], even though the verses that [the Gemara] cites are written regarding an uncircumcised person, because they derive from the single verse "according to his eating" and learn from one another for all matters; for [the law] that [if he slaughtered it] "for its eaters and not for its eaters" it is valid is because we derive [it] from "for circumcised and for uncircumcised." And specifically where he slaughtered [it] for circumcised [people] on condition that uncircumcised [people] achieve atonement did Rav Ḥisda disqualify [it], but [if] it was sprinkled for the sake of uncircumcised [people], even Rav Ḥisda concedes that it is valid, for there is no [disqualifying] intent regarding eaters during the sprinkling — as this is obvious everywhere to the redactor of the Talmud throughout our entire passage. And at the beginning of Zevachim (4a), where [the Gemara] says: "We have found slaughtering; from where [do we know] the other [blood] services? And if you should say let us derive [them] from slaughtering — what [is unique] to slaughtering is that it is disqualified [if performed] not for the sake of eaters in [the case of] the Paschal offering," it implies that there is no one who disagrees that there is no [disqualifying] intent regarding eaters during the sprinkling. And furthermore, Rav Ashi concludes that Rabba does not disagree with Rav Ḥisda on this [point]. And in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (Pesachim 78a), where it is taught [in a baraita]: "If he slaughtered it for its eaters, to sprinkle its blood not for its eaters, the Paschal offering itself is valid and a person fulfills his obligation with it," we do not read "to sprinkle its blood" [lizrok damo], rather "and its blood was sprinkled" [venizrak damo], so that it does not pose a difficulty for Rav Ḥisda — and so it is in some manuscripts. And Riba explained that [the Gemara] specifically stated "on condition that [uncircumcised people] achieve atonement" — meaning that he intended for uncircumcised [people] to achieve atonement through it; but if he did not intend [for them] to achieve atonement, rather he intended to sprinkle [the blood] in order to feed the meat to uncircumcised [people], even Rav Ḥisda concedes that it is valid, because a disqualifying intent of eating does not apply during the sprinkling, only a disqualifying [intent] of atonement. And during slaughtering specifically, if he intended to feed [it] to non-eaters or to uncircumcised [people], it is disqualified, for [during] slaughtering we certainly require [it to be] for the sake of owners who are fit to eat it, as it is written: "Each man according to his eating shall you count [for the lamb]" — and this is [what is meant by] "there is no [disqualifying] intent regarding eaters during the sprinkling."

Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:1:2.hebrew: רבה אמר כשר - תימה לר"י: נילף מק"ו דפסול משינוי בעלים! דמה הריני שוחט לשם פלוני דכשר, לזרוק דמו לשם פלוני פסול — שוחט לשם ערלים דפסול, אינו דין דלזרוק לערלים נמי פסול? וכי האי גוונא עביד בזבחים (ד' י.) קל וחומר אשלא לשמו! ותירץ ר"י, דשאני הכא דרבה יליף מקרא לקמן. ועוד אומר ר"י, דאיכא למיפרך: מה לשינוי בעלים, שכן אם זרק לשם פלוני דפסול, תאמר בשוחט לזרוק לערלים, שכן זורק לשם ערלים כשר — דאין מחשבת אוכלין בזריקה לכ"ע, כדפרישית. ואם תאמר: היא גופה נילף משינוי בעלים שיהא זורק לשם ערלים פסול? ושמא יש מיעוט למעט אוכלים מזריקה; ומיהו מ"תכוסו" לא משמע שום מיעוט, אלא מיעוט אחרינא איכא. ועוד איכא למיפרך: מה לשינוי בעלים, שכן פסול בכל הזבחים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:1:2.english: Rabba said: [It is] valid - It is astonishing to Rabbi Yitzchak: let us derive [that it is] disqualified through an a fortiori inference (kal vaḥomer) from change of owners! For just as [in the case of] "I am slaughtering for the sake of so-and-so," which is valid, [yet if he slaughters] to sprinkle its blood for the sake of so-and-so it is disqualified — [then in the case of] one who slaughters for the sake of uncircumcised [people], which is disqualified, is it not logical that [if he slaughters] to sprinkle for uncircumcised [people] it should also be disqualified? And in a similar manner, [the Gemara] in Zevachim (10a) makes an a fortiori inference regarding [slaughtering] not for its own sake! And Rabbi Yitzchak answered that here it is different, because Rabba derives [it] from a verse below. And Rabbi Yitzchak further says that one can refute [this kal vaḥomer]: What [is unique] about change of owners? [It is] that if he sprinkled [the blood] for the sake of so-and-so, it is disqualified! Can you say [the same] regarding one who slaughters to sprinkle for uncircumcised [people], when one who sprinkles for the sake of uncircumcised [people] is valid — for there is no intent regarding eaters at the sprinkling according to everyone, as I explained [above]? And if you will say: let us derive this very [law] from change of owners, that one who sprinkles for the sake of uncircumcised [people] should be disqualified? [One can answer:] Perhaps there is an exclusionary [verse] to exclude eaters from sprinkling; however, from "takhosu" [you shall make your count] no exclusion is implied, rather there is another exclusionary [verse]. And furthermore, one can refute [it]: What [is unique] about change of owners? [It is] that it is disqualified in all sacrifices.

Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:9:1.hebrew: וכי תימא ה"ה לזריקה - וכן רב אשי קאמר בסמוך: "לא שנא שחיטה ולא שנא זריקה". תימה לריב"א: כיון דזריקה קילא, דאין בה מחשבת אוכלין, היכי נילף משחיטה, ואמאי איצטריך השתא "זאת":
Tosafot on Pesachim 61b:9:1.english: And if you say the same is true of sprinkling - And similarly Rav Ashi says shortly below: "There is no difference between slaughter and sprinkling." The Riva wonders: Since sprinkling is more lenient, in that there is no intent concerning those who may eat [during sprinkling], how could we derive [sprinkling] from slaughter, and why is "this" [zot] needed now?
